import FormalConjecturesUtil
/-!
# Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Spectrum of Sequence
*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Men73] Mendès France, Michel. "Les ensembles de Bésineau."
    Séminaire Delange-Pisot-Poitou 15.1 (1973): 1-6.
-/

namespace Bugeaud04

/--
The spectrum of a sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of real numbers is the set of
irrational real numbers $\theta \in (0, 1)$ such that the sequence
$(x_n - n\theta)_{n \ge 1}$ is not uniformly distributed modulo one.
-/
def Spectrum (x : ℕ → ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
  {θ | θ ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ Irrational θ ∧
    ¬ IsEquidistributedModuloOne (fun n => x n - n * θ)}

/--
Problem 10.4. Let $\xi$ be a non-zero real number and $\alpha > 1$ be a real
number. The spectrum of the sequence $(\xi \alpha^n)_{n \ge 1}$ is at most
countable. Posed by Mendès France [Men73].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
lemma spectrum_xi_alpha_pow_countable (ξ : ℝ) (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) :
    (Spectrum (fun n => ξ * α ^ n)).Countable := by
  sorry

end Bugeaud04

reformulations.difference: Lean indexes the sequence from n = 0, whereas Bugeaud indexes it from n = 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting the initial term changes each normalized interval count by at most 1/N. Hence uniform distribution modulo one is invariant under this shift. In /workspace/review/indexing.lean, spectrum_one_based_eq proves equality with the spectrum defined using x(n+1) − (n+1)θ.

reformulations.difference: The imported uniform-distribution predicate tests closed subintervals, including singletons, rather than the usual half-open subintervals in Definition 1.1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Closed-interval equidistribution gives singleton frequency zero by taking c = d, so subtracting the upper-endpoint singleton yields the half-open criterion. Conversely, the half-open criterion bounds every singleton below 1 by intervals of arbitrarily small length, forcing its frequency to zero; fractional parts never equal 1. Adding back the upper-endpoint singleton therefore gives the closed-interval criterion.

reformulations.difference: Relative to Mendès France's original formulation on all of ℝ/ℤ, Lean excludes rational angles. This follows Bugeaud's stated definition exactly.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Represent the full-circle spectrum in [0,1). Its irrational part is precisely Bugeaud04.Spectrum, and its remaining angles form a subset of the countable set of rational reals. Thus either spectrum is at most countable if and only if the other is. This equivalence is proved for every sequence by fullSpectrum_countable_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences_checked.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations match Bugeaud's source. Checked parameter domains, quantifier scope, real-valued division and multiplication, fractional parts for negative inputs, zero denominators at the isolated initial index, occurrence-counting versus distinct-value counting, and finite/empty countability. Scratch Lean tests also show that constant zero is not equidistributed and that an irrational linear sequence can have nonempty spectrum. The equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. No contrary status update was substantiated in the consulted sources; this does not assert an exhaustive search of subsequent literature. The reviewed file remains identical to the specified commit. Detailed audit: /workspace/review/audit.md.
